frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The root ص ب ح contributes reference to al-Subh: the day's bright-light phase and, above all, its ONSET — the breaking-forth of whitish daylight that ends the dark of night. This single residue is instantiated three ways across the packet after form is subtracted: (i) the phase/time itself (nouns الصُّبْح, صَبَاح, الإِصْبَاح, adverbial صُبْحًا, participle مُصْبِحِين); (ii) a source that gives that phase's kind of light (the مِفْعَال instrument noun مِصْبَاح / مَصَابِيح 'lamp(s)'); (iii) the ENTRY into that phase, which Form IV أَصْبَحَ ('to reach/enter the morning') grammaticalizes into 'to come to be'. The distinctive core is not generic light and not generic becoming, but the daybreak — the arrival of morning brightness.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The root ص ب ح contributes reference to al-Subh: the day's bright-light phase and, above all, its ONSET — the breaking-forth of whitish daylight that ends the dark of night. This single residue is instantiated three ways across the packet after form is subtracted: (i) the phase/time itself (nouns الصُّبْح, صَبَاح, الإِصْبَاح, adverbial صُبْحًا, participle مُصْبِحِين); (ii) a source that gives that phase's kind of light (the مِفْعَال instrument noun مِصْبَاح / مَصَابِيح 'lamp(s)'); (iii) the ENTRY into that phase, which Form IV أَصْبَحَ ('to reach/enter the morning') grammaticalizes into 'to come to be'. The distinctive core is not generic light and not generic becoming, but the daybreak — the arrival of morning brightness.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every one of the 45 occurrences points back to 'morning / the coming of daylight'. The plainest cases are the dawn-nouns (الصبح 'the dawn' in 11:81, 74:34, 81:18; صباح 'morning' in 37:177; الإصباح 'daybreak' in 6:96), the 'at-daybreak' participle مصبحين (15:66, 15:83, 37:137, 68:17, 68:21), the adverbial صبحاً 'at dawn' (100:3), and صبّحهم 'he came upon them in the morning' (54:38). A large block of أصبح verbs are dawn-destruction reports where morning is transparently the moment of ruin ('and by morning they lay dead in their homes' — 7:78, 7:91, 11:67, 11:94, 29:37; الصيحة … مصبحين 15:83; فأصبحت كالصريم 68:20). Two clusters strain the reading: the LAMP words مصباح/مصابيح (24:35 x2, 41:12, 67:5), where the surviving residue is the bright LIGHT (a lamp is the instrument of morning-like light) rather than the time; and the fully bleached copular أصبح 'became' (e.g. 3:103 'you became brothers', 41:23 'you became of the losers', 5:52/5:53/49:6 'they/you became regretful/losers'), where context shows no dawn at all and only the 'come-to-be' aspect remains. Both are reconcilable through a prototype: the root always names the bright daytime-light phase, given either as light (lamp) or as onset (become) — but in these two clusters the morning-invariant is present by lexical/grammatical inheritance, not visibly in the verse.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM does heavy lifting and must be subtracted. Form IV أَصْبَحَ is a paradigmatic 'verb of becoming' (alongside أمسى evening, أضحى forenoon, بات night, ظلّ daytime); the copular 'become' function belongs to Form IV, while the ROOT contributes only which time-of-day phase is being entered — 'morning'. Thus 'became brothers' (3:103) = FORM(enter-the-phase→become) + ROOT(morning-phase). مِصْبَاح is a مِفْعَال instrument noun: FORM supplies 'instrument for X', ROOT supplies X = morning-light. صُبْحًا (100:3) is adverbial-accusative time; صَبَّحَ (II) is 'do-to-someone at morning' (attack-at-dawn), FORM supplying the transitive/timed frame. Once these are removed, the recurring root residue is uniformly 'the morning-brightness / its arrival'. CONSTRUCTION notes: أصبح + predicate = inchoative copula; أصبح + فِى دِيارهم جاثمين = timed resultative in punishment narratives; participle مصبحين = circumstantial 'while entering morning'.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 3:103 — فَأَصْبَحْتُم بِنِعْمَتِهِۦٓ إِخْوَٰنًا ('by His grace you became brothers'). There is no dawn, no morning marker, and no light in the context; أصبح functions as a pure inchoative copula ('came to be'). The 'morning' residue is not demonstrably present in the verse — it survives only paradigmatically (أصبح vs أمسى) and etymologically. The lamp cluster (24:35, 41:12, 67:5) is the parallel counterexample from the opposite direction: there the residue is 'bright light', with the time-of-morning component absent. Together these two clusters show the root's invariant splits — one branch keeps the LIGHT, the other keeps the ONSET/TRANSITION — so no single element is transparently visible in literally every occurrence.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Competing hypothesis: the root's core is generic 'to become / transition into a state', with 'morning' being merely one derived scene. This is rejected because it inverts the derivation: cross-linguistically and within the Arabic paradigm the copular sense is demonstrably a Form-IV grammaticalization of a concrete time-of-day verb, and the many purely nominal/temporal occurrences (الصبح, صباح, الإصباح, صبحاً, مصبحين, مصباح) have NO 'become' sense — they are irreducibly about morning-light. A generic 'become' core cannot generate 'lamp' or 'dawn' nouns. A second competing hypothesis makes the core generic 'light/brightness' (making مصباح primary); rejected because it under-specifies — the root is distinctively the MORNING light-phase (hence أصبح 'morning-become' contrasts with أمسى 'evening-become'), not light in general.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Residue is distinctive against nearest roots: فَجَر (dawn as the CLEAVING/bursting of the horizon — process of splitting, cf. فالق الإصباح at 6:96 pairs both) vs ص ب ح which names the resulting bright morning-phase; نور / ضوء (generic light / ray, non-temporal) vs ص ب ح's specifically diurnal morning-light; شرق (rising/east, source-direction of light) vs ص ب ح (the light-state that ensues); أمسى / أضحى (become-at-evening / -forenoon) — same Form-IV becoming template, differing ONLY by the root's time-phase, which is exactly the load-bearing distinctive residue of ص ب ح. The lamp sense مصباح is still distinctive (a morning-bright-quality light) rather than mere سراج.
unresolved_cases: Bleached copular أصبح with no contextual dawn: 3:103 (إخواناً), 41:23 (من الخاسرين), 5:52 (نادمين), 5:53 (خاسرين), 49:6 (نادمين), 61:14 (ظاهرين), 5:30/5:31 (من الخاسرين/النادمين), 5:102 (كافرين), 28:82 (يقولون), 30:17 (تصبحون, though here paired with تمسون it recovers the literal morning) — in these the morning-invariant is inherited paradigmatically/etymologically, not visible in the verse.
Lamp cluster مصباح/مصابيح: 24:35 (x2), 41:12, 67:5 — residue reduces to 'bright light-source'; the time-of-morning component is absent, present only as the light-quality of the root.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single distinctive residue — 'al-Subh, the bright morning-light phase and its onset' — accounts for all 45 occurrences under a principled radial/prototype model, and the two extension patterns are systematic, not ad hoc: (a) instrument-noun lexicalization مِفْعَال → مصباح (the light-of-morning as a source), and (b) Form-IV grammaticalization أصبح → 'become' (entering the morning-phase), where 'morning' remains the distinctive paradigm feature separating أصبح from أمسى/أضحى. No occurrence contradicts the residue (none makes the root itself denote night, evening, or darkness), so inconsistent_refs is empty. Strength is capped at MODERATE, not STRONG, because in the fully bleached copular أصبح (paradigm case 3:103) and in the lamp cluster the invariant is carried by inheritance rather than shown transparently in context, and because the root's invariant bifurcates — one branch preserves the LIGHT component, the other the ONSET/TRANSITION component — so no one surface element is visible in literally every verse. Under the strict 'demonstrably present in EVERY occurrence' reading these two clusters are the honest weak points; under a prototype reading with form fully subtracted they reconcile. I therefore report PREFERRED/MODERATE rather than STRONG, and rather than UNRESOLVED, since a coherent, distinctive, falsifiable single contribution does hold across the full set.

adversarial_verification.notes: Full coverage verified (45 occ; form_inventory sums to 45). The daybreak/onset residue is overtly present in the phase/time nouns (100:3, 11:81x2, 37:177, 74:34, 81:18, 6:96), the muSbiHin participles (15:66, 15:83, 37:137, 68:17, 68:21), the literal Form IV pair tuSbiHun (30:17), and V(II) SabbaHahum bukratan (54:38); the miSbAH/maSAbiH lamp uses (24:35x2, 41:12, 67:5) map more loosely as 'source of light.' The refutation lies in the bleached copular Form IV block (akhawat kana). In the 18 listed occurrences aSbaHa/tuSbiHu = simply 'became/come to be' with NO morning, dawn, or light content in the occurrence itself (e.g. 5:30 'became one of the losers', 3:103 'became brothers', 22:63 'the earth becomes green', 18:42 'began turning his hands', 28:10 'the heart became empty'). After subtracting Form IV, the required root residue is EMPTY, violating the 'non-empty residue in EVERY occurrence' rule. The proposal's own phrasing — Form IV 'grammaticalizes into to come to be' — concedes the semantic bleaching. Distinctiveness fails: in these uses the residue is indistinguishable from generic inchoativity and from the evening-root copula amsa (30:17 tumsun) / Sara — every 'become' verb encodes onset, so 'onset' is not distinctive. Reliance on the morning etymology to recover the residue is inadmissible (etymology != evidence per hard rules). The dawn-destruction narratives (7:78, 7:91, 11:67, 11:94, 29:37) and 28:18/28:82/68:20 survive only via CONTEXT supplying morning, never the word, so they are marginal rather than clean support. Under non-negotiable root unity, 18 unreconciled confirmed occurrences mean universal presence does NOT hold. The claim is falsifiable (these occurrences falsify it) but the grammaticalization move is used to immunize it against exactly this refutation.
